Both halves are supported: the corpus carries visible internal difference, and no retrieved instrument converts that difference into an ordering this repository can defend.

claim: Family-book location is an attestation fact and this unit treats it as one. A stanza is in book 2 or it is not; that is a property of the arrangement (DATE 3) and is not disturbed by anything found here. The separate claim that family-book material is EARLIER is a method claim resting on other instruments, and under Arnold's it does not hold in the form usually stated.
locator: DA-M-004; A1-stratum-by-book-padas.csv. Books 5, 6 and 7 carry Arnold-late shares of 31.05%, 30.32% and 31.25% against book 1's 33.95%; books 8 and 9 carry 4.40% and 5.82%, the lowest in the corpus
notes: The instruction this unit was given is that the two are different claims and the second does not erase the first. That is exactly what the numbers show. Note what is NOT claimed: that books 8 and 9 are therefore early. A metrical instrument that ranks them earliest is more likely telling us about their metres - book 9 is 73.3% Normal, book 8 is 49.2% Strophic and has no Cretic pada at all - than about their dates. STRENGTHENED 2026-09-09: DA-M-025 shows that at the hymn unit the relation between book number and Arnold-late share is measurable and SCOPE-DEPENDENT - positive over all books, negative over books 1-9, positive again within the family books. That is a further reason to keep the attestation fact and the chronological inference apart, and it is not a licence to read any of those signs as a date.

claim: Books 8 and 9 are 'internally complicated' in a sense Arnold's instrument does not capture. On stratum entropy they are among the LESS heterogeneous books (normalised entropy 0.613 and 0.562 against book 1's 0.972 and book 10's 0.815), and book 9 has no lowercase code anywhere.
notes: Constitution 4.A calls 8 and 9 internally complicated. Under this instrument they are the most metrically uniform books in the corpus. Either the complication is of a kind metre does not see - book 9 is a ritual collection defined by its subject, book 8 by its strophic forms - or the claim needs restating. PROVISIONAL: this record cannot yet say which, and both readings are live.

claim: Arnold's late-marking receives real support from one instrument that is neither Arnold nor entangled with another: Grassmann 1876-7 flags stanzas that sit in Arnold's late strata at 2.34 times the base rate within books 1-9, i.e. with book 10 removed.
notes: This is the finding that cuts AGAINST the unit's framing, and it is reported as prominently as the findings that cut with it. TWO LIMITS, the second added 2026-09-09 after adversarial review. First, it is one instrument, from 1876-7, whose marking criterion is undocumented in the bundle (DA-M-020), and it is not a replication. Second, and more serious: Grassmann's independence from Arnold was measured only COLUMN AGAINST COLUMN inside stanza_properties.json, which cannot see whether Arnold 1905 read Grassmann 1876-7 - and Grassmann's edition is one of the works Arnold's generation of metrical chronology was built on. That is untested and untestable here (DA-M-023, DEP-036, BF-029). The claim that Arnold's strata rest on nothing outside Arnold remains one this record does not make; the claim that Grassmann corroborates them INDEPENDENTLY is now explicitly marked as unestablished.

claim: The four non-Arnold columns of stanza_properties are not four instruments. Oldenberg and Wuest share 641 of their 699 and 709 flagged stanzas (Jaccard 0.836), so they count as approximately one; Witzel overlaps each at Jaccard ~0.48; Grassmann is the only column distinct from all others.
notes: VERIFIED as a measurement of overlap. The 2026-09-07 manifest called these 'four further scholars' judgements ... from different evidence (style, grammar, textual criticism, history)' and asked whether they agree with Arnold. Half the answer is that they are not four, and the source-independence rule required measuring that before using them.

claim: The Hellwig, Scarlata and Widmer 2021 result is NOT a universal falsification of Rigvedic relative chronology, and the record states what it is. What was tested: whether allomorphic linguistic features previously claimed to bear stratification signals support the proposed stratifications, once metrical positioning, prosodic structure and content are controlled for. What was found: they do not, and a cluster analysis over the same data favours a special position for book 10 while finding overall between-book differences 'not substantial'.

notes: Three things it does not establish, none of which the abstract claims: that the Rigveda is chronologically homogeneous; that no relative chronology exists; and that its result extends beyond allomorphy to other evidence classes. WITHDRAWN 2026-09-09 after adversarial review: an earlier version of this row also claimed it does not establish 'that Arnold's metrical stratification in particular is unsupported', on the ground that metrical positioning is among the controls. That exculpation went beyond the abstract. The abstract says the allomorph distributions do not support 'ANY of the proposed stratifications', the paper is titled 'Reassessing Rigvedic Strata', and Arnold's is the canonical proposed stratification - so whether Arnold's is inside 'any' is precisely what the abstract cannot settle, and this record must not settle it in the instrument's favour. It is UNDETERMINED and stays that way until the full text is read. HOLD-008.

claim: The 'perfect audio recording' framing is refuted by the bundle itself and does not need an argument. The tradition transmits two complete forms of its own text that differ at essentially every stanza (median character similarity 0.913), and a modern metrical restoration differs from the recited form at 72.04% of stanzas.

claim: The opposite framing is refuted by the same fact from the other side. A tradition that had rewritten its text would not preserve, inside itself, a second analysis of that text which disagrees with the first at nine tenths of its stanzas. Whatever the Padapatha is, it is not a smoothing.
notes: PROVISIONAL because it is an inference from the existence of the Padapatha to the intention behind it, and this repository has retrieved nothing on Sakalya, nothing on the pratisakhyas and nothing on Panini (DA-D-006). The inference is available; it is not evidenced.

claim: Later sandhi and contraction demonstrably obscure an older metrical form, and the effect is corpus-wide rather than a property of late material. 72.04% of stanzas differ between the transmitted and the restored text; in 69.01% of those the restoration is longer; and the differing share is HIGHEST in the stratum Arnold calls Archaic (77.20%).
notes: Constitution 4.A item 9, measured. The direction matters: the Samhitapatha applies ONE phonology across material the same corpus's own instrument assigns to five different periods. That is the strongest single piece of evidence in this unit that transmission normalised something, and it is also the noise floor any metrical dating instrument has to read through.

claim: What was preserved extraordinarily well and what may already have changed can be separated in this corpus, and the separation is visible without any chronological assumption. What survived: the syllable count and the accents, well enough that a metrical restoration is possible at all and that a word-analysis can be aligned to the recited text at 91% of its segments. What did not: the boundary phonology, which the Samhitapatha overwrites uniformly.
notes: Constitution 4.A's last two items. PROVISIONAL because 'well enough that a restoration is possible' is a judgement about van Nooten and Holland's method, and their edition was not read - only its output was compared (SRC-078). The direction of the finding is not in doubt; its strength is.

claim: Arnold's stratum assignment is strongly but not wholly predicted by the surface metre label: Cramer's V = 0.5314, and the metre label explains 29.19% of the stratum's entropy. That is consistent both with Arnold having used finer metrical facts than the label records and with the stratum being largely a metrical-genre partition. The measurement does not separate the two.
notes: Opened 2026-09-09 to carry the reading that DA-M-006 previously carried as VERIFIED. The earlier reading ran one way only - 'so he was using finer metrical facts' - on the weakest of the available statistics. The stronger statistics support the confound as readily as the defence, and both readings are now stated. This is the confound Hellwig, Scarlata and Widmer report controlling for, which is why their control for metrical positioning does not settle anything about metre in this repository's favour (DA-008).
